DEFENSIVES LEADCyclicals -2.3% vs defensives on the month
Rotation ReadCitrini · claude

The one thing to own right now is secular tech and biotech, and you should stay hedged against the cyclical recovery the Q3 rally tried to price. XLK leads the sector table at +6.56% over the past month and +36.08% year to date, with XLV second at +2.53% and a far quieter +10.60% YTD.

XLE sits at +2.29% for the month but +44.60% YTD, and then there is a cliff: XLP at -0.01%, XLU at -0.45%, XLI at -0.46%, XLY at -0.51%. The bottom of the monthly table is financials and communications: XLF at -3.47%, XLC at -3.15%, XLRE at -2.78%.

The cyclical trade is bleeding, not pulling back toward strength.

Secular tech leadership versus a cyclical and small-cap complex that is rolling over, with breadth ratios screaming narrow market.

BULL

XLK at +6.56% and cyber at +13.20% show money still concentrating in higher-growth, longer-duration assets, and XLE at +2.29% keeps the reflation trade from fully dying.

BEAR

XLF at -3.47%, XLC at -3.15%, and XLRE at -2.78% over the past month say the cyclical and rate-sensitive engines are stalling, and IWM/QQQ at a z-score of -2.43 (bottom 2% of its yearly range) confirms small caps are being left for dead while the index rides mega-cap tech.

TELL

Watch XLK versus XLE. If tech leadership starts to narrow into only a few cyber and AI-infra names while XLE cannot reclaim its monthly gain, the narrow-breadth read wins and you keep sizing into secular tech and biotech.

The most useful extremes here are not the tech leadership ratios; they are the haven and breadth ratios that have run to truly uncommon levels. Three credit and rates ratios sit in the top 97% to 98% of their yearly range: SHY/TLT at a z-score of 2.61, BKLN/HYG at 2.51, and SPY/TLT at 2.19.

SHY/TLT at 2.61 means short-duration Treasuries have never been this expensive against long bonds in the past year, which is a pure long-end duration aversion trade that is getting stretched. BKLN/HYG at 2.51 has floating-rate loans at a record premium to high yield, and JNK/TLT at a z-score of 2.18 says the entire credit complex is expensive against long Treasuries.

On the other side, IWM/QQQ at -2.43 (bottom 2% of its yearly range) and EFA/SPY at -2.22 (bottom 0%) are extreme readings that look more like trend than mispricing; you would be catching a falling knife to lean against small-cap and international weakness. The one ratio that looks like a genuine mean-reversion candidate is TLT/IEF at a z-score of -2.22 (bottom 4%), where long bonds are cheap against intermediate Treasuries and any dovish shift in the front end could force a violent steepening trade that would pull XLRE, XLU, and XLF up with it.
